title: Execution-plan stamping to ensure safe CUDA graph replay
creator: Marco DeLuca
description:
Background: We intermittently observe nondeterministic failures and subtle correctness drift when replaying CUDA graphs for concurrent multi-stream decode workloads. Root causes include differing kernel selection paths between capture and replay (kernel fallback/quantization variants), reordered prefill windows, and transient KV-cache state that is not reflected in the graph capture. These manifest as token mismatches or rare segfaults under high concurrency.

Proposal: Implement an execution-plan stamping mechanism that records a compact fingerprint (stamped metadata) of the decisions made during capture and validates it at replay time. The stamp includes: kernel selection ids (per-layer), quantization/packing mode, attention kernel variant id, prefill window hash, and a lightweight KV-cache epoch marker. On replay, the runtime compares stamps and either accepts, fast-fails with a deterministic fallback path, or triggers an automated recapture if allowed by policy. Stamping is designed to be low-overhead (<=2% token latency at worst) and to provide deterministic detection for replay divergence.

Design highlights:
- Stamp format is a fixed-length byte vector and versioned so future fields can be appended without breaking past captures.
- Kernel ids are negotiated from the kernel catalog at capture time and stored as IDs rather than pointers.
- Prefill window hash uses a rolling checksum of the token-length distribution and key prefill metadata (not the token bytes) to avoid PII/exposure.
- Replay-time policy: strict mode (production-critical) will fast-fail to a cold-exec fallback and emit a high-severity alert; permissive mode will attempt a recapture if runtime capacities permit.
- Integration with scheduler: capture stamping will be a pre-step before cudaGraph capture commit. The scheduler will use stamps to avoid routing a replay to an incompatible kernel pool.

Trade-offs considered:
- Recording full runtime state (tensor contents) would be more accurate but far too expensive. Stamping trades complete determinism for a compact, high-signal fingerprint.
- Recapture on mismatch increases tail latency for the affected request but avoids silent correctness drift. We will default to fast-fail for high-SLA customers and recapture for lower tiers.

Expected benefits:
- Deterministic detection of capture/replay divergence, reducing silent token-level regressions.
- Safer rollouts of kernel selector improvements and quantization heuristics.
- Reduced incident MTTR due to clearer provenance in capture metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Stamp produced on 100% of captures in the new staging runtime without >3% QPS regression
Replay compares stamp and logs mismatch with clear reason (kernel id mismatch, prefill hash mismatch, kv-epoch mismatch),
Strict-mode fast-fail occurs and triggers alerting in <=50ms after mismatch detection
Recapture flow successfully re-captures and serves identical outputs for a set of 1k deterministic fuzz tests
Benchmark: end-to-end median token latency increase from stamping <=2% and p99 increase <=5% under representative load
tasks: Design stamp schema and versioning proposal (API & on-disk layout)
Extend kernel catalog to export stable kernel ids and mapping table
Implement stamp generation in capture path and fast-compare in replay path
Add scheduler integration to avoid incompatible kernel pool routing
Build unit + integration tests including deterministic fuzz harness
Add observability: metrics, structured logs, and dashboard for stamp mismatches
Create rollout/feature flag gating and runtime policies per-customer tier
test_plan: Unit tests for schema encode/decode and version compatibility
Replay mismatch simulation tests by mutating kernel id table and prefill hash
Deterministic fuzz: run 10k capture/replay cycles across model size/quantization combos and assert no silent token divergence
Load test: stage at 30% of production QPS to verify latency and mismatch rates
Chaos test: inject kernel pool failures to verify fallback policies and alerting
rollout_plan: Enable in internal staging cluster for 1 week with full logging
Enable in canary subset of customers (low impact) with strict=off for 48 hours
Enable strict-mode for high-SLA customers after monitoring for 72 hours
Full production enable with monitoring + auto-recapture policies after successful canary
risks: False positives: noisy mismatches due to non-deterministic scheduler behavior could cause unnecessary fallbacks
Performance overhead: stamping adds CPU work on capture thread and extra checks on replay
Operational complexity: need to maintain kernel id compatibility and migrations across releases
Privacy: must ensure prefill hash does not leak input tokens or sensitive info
notes: Initial PoC shows clear detection of kernel-selection regressions introduced by kernel-selector v2 in internal tests
We will not store raw token or KV state in stamps; only metadata fingerprints
Follow-up work: extend stamp to include memory-layout hints for heterogeneous GPU pools

2026-03-03 Alex Chen: Scheduler integration reviewed. Need to ensure router exposes kernel pool fingerprint before routing decision — added dependency to ENG-61234.
